guide_enrichment.narrative: We are not dismissing Army’s offense to make the case for Louisiana Tech. Our efficiency numbers give Army an advantage against Louisiana Tech’s defense both on the ground and through the air. That concern has real context: Army averaged 394 rushing yards through two games, and Cale Hellums returned after starting 10 games in 2025, when he rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns. Army also lists five seniors across its first-team offensive line, giving the unit considerable experience up front.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Army’s multidimensional offense against Louisiana Tech’s defense. Hellums completed 9 of 10 passes with two touchdowns against South Florida, while Army did not throw an interception in its first two games. We need to see whether Louisiana Tech can contain the rushing attack without giving Hellums efficient opportunities through the air. That matchup is the main reason our broader preference for Louisiana Tech does not create enough value for us at the current price.

recent_game.fact: Army lost 28-24 to South Florida on Sept. 12, falling to 1-1 overall and 0-1 in the American Conference.
Against South Florida, quarterback Cale Hellums completed 9 of 10 passes for 91 yards and two touchdowns; his .900 completion percentage was a career high.
Running back Godspower Nwawuihe led Army against South Florida with 20 carries for 98 yards and scored a 10-yard fourth-quarter rushing touchdown.
Slotback Zach Mundell caught three passes against South Florida, including a 24-yard touchdown, and completed a 37-yard pass to Godspower Nwawuihe.

opponent_notes.fact: Army is scheduled to play at Louisiana Tech on Oct. 3, 2026, at 7:30 p.m. Eastern.

quarterback.fact: Senior Cale Hellums is Army's first-team quarterback, followed on the Sept. 20 depth chart by sophomore Bryson Luter and sophomore Ethan Washington.
Hellums returned as Army's starting quarterback in 2026 after making 10 starts and appearing in every game in 2025.
Hellums rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025; the 18 rushing touchdowns were second-most in an Army season.
Through Army's first two games of 2026, Hellums had 150 passing yards, 142 rushing yards and four total touchdowns.
In the season opener against Bryant, Hellums rushed seven times for 87 yards and two touchdowns and completed 4 of 9 passes for 59 yards.

offensive_personnel.fact: Army's first-team offensive line on the Sept. 20 depth chart was left tackle Henry Appleton, left guard Kyle Kloska, center Brady Small, right guard Paolo Gennarelli and right tackle Teddy Williams; all five are seniors.
Godspower Nwawuihe is listed as Army's first-team running back ahead of Jake Rendina and Carson Smith.
Army identified Nwawuihe as its feature back in 2026 after his breakout performance in the 2025 Fenway Bowl.
Samari Howard, Zach Mundell and David Clerk are the top three slotbacks on Army's Sept. 20 depth chart.
Mundell's 2026 opener against Bryant was only his second game since 2023; he rushed four times for a team-high 105 yards and two touchdowns.
Parker Poloskey is Army's first-team tight end, with Tex Brannan and Brian Dyer behind him.
Army's listed first-team wide receivers are Brady Anderson, Tobi Olawole and Kavon Pointer.

defensive_personnel.fact: Army's listed starting defensive line consists of Dillon Stowers at defensive tackle, Kody Harris-Miller at nose tackle and Jack Bousum at defensive end.
Army's first-team linebackers are outside linebacker Noah Nixon and inside linebackers Jaquavious Moss and Elijah Walton.
Army's listed starting secondary consists of nickel Zane Tallman, cornerbacks Jaydan Mayes and Jaxon Hammond, strong safety Caleb Williams and free safety Stephen Nnadozie.
Elijah Walton and Jaquavious Moss shared Army's team lead with 12 tackles each through two games.
Dillon Stowers led Army with one sack through two games, while Zane Tallman had the team's only forced fumble.

coaching_changes.fact: Cody Worley is in his seventh season as Army's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, while Daryl Dixon is in his 11th season as defensive coordinator.
John Holt joined Army in 2026 as co-offensive line coach, working alongside third-year co-offensive line coach Cheston Blackshear.
Jamere Hogue is Army's first-year defensive line coach, and Munir Prince is its first-year cornerbacks coach.
H.T. Kinney joined Army in 2026 as senior offensive analyst.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Army averaged 394.0 rushing yards, 497.5 total yards and 41.5 points per game.
Army led the FBS in rushing offense at 394.0 yards per game and ranked 20th nationally in total offense at 497.5 yards per game through three weeks.
Army had not thrown an interception through its first two games and averaged 34:22 in time of possession.
Army was tied for sixth nationally with 25 rushing plays of at least 10 yards through three weeks.
Zach Mundell, Godspower Nwawuihe and Cale Hellums each had at least 140 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns through Army's first two games.
Army produced 648 total yards and 569 rushing yards in its 59-3 season-opening win over Bryant; both totals ranked fourth in program single-game history.
Army averaged 10.0 yards per rush against Bryant, its highest single-game mark since averaging 10.9 against Fordham in 2017.

defensive_context.fact: Through two games, Army allowed 15.5 points and 267.0 total yards per game.
Army allowed 98.5 rushing yards and 168.5 passing yards per game through its first two contests.
Army had allowed 30 first downs through two games, the third-fewest nationally at that point.

special_teams.fact: James Wagenseller is Army's first-team punter, Dawson Jones is the first-team kicker and kickoff specialist, and Owen Walter is the first-team long snapper.
Samari Howard and Jaydan Mayes are listed as co-primary kickoff returners, while Lloyd Benson III is the first-team punt returner.
Army averaged 47.6 yards per punt through two games, ranking third nationally.
Lloyd Benson III averaged 18.7 yards per punt return through two games, ranking 16th nationally.

series_context.fact: Army defeated Louisiana Tech in the Radiance Technologies Independence Bowl following the 2024 season.

other_relevant.fact: Army entered the Temple game week with a 1-1 record after finishing 7-6 and winning the Fenway Bowl in 2025.
Jeff Monken was in his 13th season as Army's head coach with a 90-64 record at the school.
